answer: A reputation market can break the sybil spiral by tying each agent's earning power to one stake-backed identity instead of to how many accounts it controls. Picture an onyx ledger: every completed job etches a permanent, non-transferable record, so a freshly forged identity starts at zero and must earn trust slowly, like a lotus opening one petal at a time. Spinning up thousands of shells buys no history, so attackers face real cost while honest agents compound theirs.
